newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, U.S. in close contact on Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: France, U.S. in close contact on Zaire force.

text.p: Paris and Washington are in constant contact about France's proposal for a multinational force to avert a humanitarian disaster among a million refugees displaced by fighting in Zaire, officials said on Thursday.
French spokesman Yves Doutriaux said the latest top-level contact was between French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher late on Wednesday.

"The United States asked France for additional details on its proposals. Mr de Charette reminded the United States of the urgent need for a joint solution...including U.S. participation," Doutriaux said.
A senior French Defence Ministry official said an international force could start moving into the area three or four days after getting a green light from the United Nations.

But officials in Paris were vague about who was ready to join such a force apart from France, Spain and Ethiopia. The three are the only countries which have so far said they are willing to contribute troops to create "security zones" where refugees could be cared for.
The United States, while leaning towards providing logistical support for such a force, does not intend to offer ground troops, senior officials said in Washington.

De Charette accused the international community of being spineless on Wednesday, venting French frustration at the poor response to the Paris suggestion of a multinational force which was endorsed at an African summit in Nairobi on Tuesday.

France insists all major nations must participate in the force, which would help to get relief to more than a million refugees in eastern Zaire left without food by the fighting between Zairean troops and Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels.
Specialists said moving the force quickly would depend largely on whether the United States would put giant Galaxy and Starlifter military transport aicraft at its disposal.
France has vast experience in moving small units quickly to Africa but does not have enough big transport planes for large-scale operations.

Sending armoured personnel carriers and heavy lorries into Rwanda and the Central African Republic for recent French operations was made possible only by chartering huge Antonov transports from Ukraine.

Before the fall of the Iron Curtain and the availability of Ukrainian planes to take military vehicles, French paratroopers routinely commandeered any vehicles they could find when they reached target areas, sometimes going off into operations aboard schoolbuses.
Media reports said Paris wanted to take control of the airports in Goma and Bukavu, seized by Tutsi rebels, to allow relief workers to resume aid to refugee camps.
The rebels, who are holding a swathe of eastern Zaire, said they wanted an African force to protect the refugees and opposed intervention by troops from outside the region, including any from France.
France intervened in the area in 1994 to end ethnic massacres, drawing charges from its allies that it was seeking to further its interests and from Tutsi-ruled Rwanda that it was protecting Hutus.
